## Patchset 2's fail-closed scan broke a precheck test; fixed structurally

`make verify` on patchset 2 came back RC=2 with one failure:
`tests/unit/test_close_duration_instrumentation.py::test_completion_precheck_threads_one_collector_through_pass_and_sidecar`.

**Root cause — two of this patchset's own changes interacting.** The blocking-finding fix
makes `_refuse_open_sunset_marker` run unconditionally, so every precheck test now reaches
the marker scan. Advisory 1's fix made `_marker_lines` fail closed, but its benign branch
matched only the stderr text `not a git repository`. That test passes `/code`, a path that
does not exist, and `git grep` reports a MISSING directory with the same exit status (128)
and different prose:

```
fatal: cannot change to '/code': No such file or directory
```

so the scan raised `RuntimeError` and the precheck died.

**The fix is structural, not a wider string match.** On an unexpected `git grep` status the
scan now asks git whether a repository is reachable at all — a new `_has_repository` helper
running `git -C <root> rev-parse --git-dir`. No repository means no tracked set, which is an
empty answer; a repository that IS there and failed to scan still raises. Telling the two
apart by git's own structural answer rather than by its prose means a reworded or localized
message cannot turn a failed scan into a silent pass, which was the whole point of advisory 1.

**Test changes.**

- New `test_a_code_root_that_does_not_exist_yields_no_markers` — the regression proof.
  RED-proved: restoring the string-matching branch makes it fail with
  `RuntimeError` at `sunset_markers.py:116`.
- `test_a_failed_scan_raises_instead_of_passing_the_close` previously monkeypatched
  `subprocess.run` to return 128 for EVERY call, which would now also fake away the
  repository probe and let the guard excuse itself. Its fake now answers by argv:
  `rev-parse` → 0, `grep` → 128. That is a more faithful model of the case it names — a real
  repository whose grep failed — so the test actually exercises the raising path.

`make lint` RC=0 (`active=647 new=32 increased=0 stale=0`, exit 0), `make typecheck` RC=0
across 754 source files, and the 30 tests across `test_sunset_markers.py`,
`test_sunset_marker_close_gate_independence.py`, and `test_close_duration_instrumentation.py`
all pass. Full `make verify` restarted.

## Patch set 2 pushed to 3261 (`6a1783c1f4a`) — verify green, reply posted

`make verify` RC=0: 20497 passed / 27 skipped (default tier, 1:21:17), 203 passed / 3 skipped
(integration tier, 5:26). 0 FAILED or ERROR lines.

This is the run that confirms the regression fix. The previous attempt failed
`test_completion_precheck_threads_one_collector_through_pass_and_sidecar` because two of my own
patch-set-2 changes interacted: making `_refuse_open_sunset_marker` unconditional routed every
precheck test through the marker scan, and the fail-closed guard in `_marker_lines` was matching
git's stderr text. `git grep` reports a missing directory and a non-repository with the **same
exit status 128** and different prose, so the placeholder root `/code` raised instead of
returning no markers.

Fixed structurally rather than by widening the string match: a `_has_repository` helper runs
`git -C <root> rev-parse --git-dir`, and the scan consults it only on an unexpected status. No
repository reachable → empty answer; repository present but the scan failed → still raises. A
reworded or localized git message cannot turn a failed scan into a silent pass.

The regression also exposed a bad test fake. `test_a_failed_scan_raises_instead_of_passing_the_close`
monkeypatched `subprocess.run` to return 128 for *every* call, so once the fix added the
`rev-parse` probe that same fake would have driven the guard down its benign branch and the test
would have silently stopped exercising the raising path. Its fake now answers by argv —
`rev-parse` → 0, `grep` → 128 — which models a real repository whose grep failed.

Awaiting `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` on patch set 2.

MERGED. Gerrit 3261 patchset 2 (`6a1783c1f4ad96d0b0173bdd396cd829160dbe02`) earned
LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, 0 unresolved comments, and was submitted
revision-scoped. Change status is MERGED.

AC VERIFICATION against the merged tree, from the `impl-d68f` worktree at that commit.

AC1 — grammar, one test per case. 4 tests added to tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py by
this commit: test_a_reason_naming_no_sunset_ticket_does_not_admit,
test_a_bare_single_quad_does_not_admit, test_every_resolvable_id_form_admits (covering the
alias, two-quad and four-quad forms in one parametrization), and
test_removing_a_mechanism_still_passes. MET.

AC2 — close precheck, one test per case. tests/unit/test_sunset_markers.py is new (225
lines, 17 tests). The three named cases are
test_the_close_is_refused_while_a_marker_names_the_ticket,
test_the_close_succeeds_once_the_marker_is_removed, and
test_a_ticket_named_by_no_marker_is_unaffected, with the file-plus-line requirement pinned
separately by test_the_refusal_names_the_file_and_line_so_it_is_actionable. MET.

AC3 — two invariants. The shrink-only asymmetry is test_removing_a_mechanism_still_passes;
the no-CI-environment invariant is test_the_scan_needs_no_ci_environment. MET.

AC4 — marker migration. Verified with the ratchet's OWN harvest rather than a text scan:
`markers_for(Path('.'))` from scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py, which harvests only
locations a detector actually reported. Result on the merged tree: 36 real-site markers,
36 naming a resolvable sunset ticket, 0 with a blank reason, 0 nonblank-but-unresolvable.
No real-site marker lacks a resolvable id. MET in substance.

A COUNT NOTE, because the AC's numbers no longer describe the tree. The AC says "14 ... with
the remaining 76 (75 id + 1 alias)", i.e. 90 total, and the Measurement base records that
the 90/75/1/14 split came from "parsing every site with `parse_marker`" at `346a76f1c87`.
That method counts every LINE matching the marker regex across all tracked files, which
includes prose in AGENTS.md and docs/architecture.md, docstrings in markers.py and
sunset_markers.py that quote the form, string literals inside compare.py and
check_mechanism_delta.py, and test fixtures. Re-running that broad method on the merged
tree gives 114 such lines, 88 of them naming a resolvable ticket. The ratchet's own harvest
gives 36. The two numbers measure different things; only the 36 is the set the ratchet can
admit a mechanism from, and it is clean. The AC's substance — no real-site marker without a
resolvable id — holds; its literal arithmetic was measured by a looser method against an
older tree and should not be read as a current census.

AC5 — `make verify`. RC=0 on this tree: 20497 passed / 27 skipped in the default tier
(1:21:17), 203 passed / 3 skipped in the integration tier (5:26), 0 FAILED and 0 ERROR.
That run included the regression that broke the prior attempt
(test_completion_precheck_threads_one_collector_through_pass_and_sidecar), now passing. MET.

Closing.

compiled_state.description:
## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`, authorized at full scope by the operator on 2026-11-02.
Deliverable 2. Depends on `fe94-2e22-ea9e-46f7`, which establishes the net-mechanism
criterion this story's own change must satisfy.

## The gap

A mechanism admitted by a `# mechanism-ok:` marker is admitted FOREVER. Measured at
`origin/main` `346a76f1c87`:

- The grammar is `scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:20` (`_MARKER_RE`), separators at
  `:23` — `("—", "--", "-", ":")` — capture at `:42-43`. Three fields: kind, name, reason.
  It is ONE LINE: `parse_marker` (`:37-44`) reads a single line, `_record` (`:66-68`)
  stores that line's reason, so continuation lines are invisible to the ratchet.
- `compare.py:89` partitions `counters.new` against the harvested markers, `:91-92`
  emitting the `admitted` line, so a nonblank reason admits the key. A blank reason becomes
  an error in `_blank_marker_errors` (`:58`, called at `:87`) reaching the exit at `:99`.
- Nothing parses a ticket id out of the reason, nor checks that a referenced ticket
  exists, is open, or ever closes.

So `# mechanism-ok: env_var REBAR_X — remove after the migration` blesses the mechanism
permanently: the migration closes, the marker stays, the ratchet never looks again. The
admission is a one-way door with no expiry.

## The convention exists but is not enforced

Every tracked file was parsed with the ratchet's own `parse_marker`, excluding the
grammar's 6 definition sites (`markers.py`, `compare.py`, `check_mechanism_delta.py`,
`test_mechanism_delta.py`, `docs/architecture.md`, `AGENTS.md`):

- **90 real admission markers.** 3 further hits quote the grammar rather than admit
  anything, so are excluded: `Makefile:289`, ADR `0112:232`,
  `src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:213`.
- **75 already name a two- or four-quad id**, e.g. `1e24-bfc0` on the Gerrit-retry
  `ci_gate` markers in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`.
- **1 names an ALIAS only**: `src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock.py:78` cites
  `metaphoric-late-creature`. An alias IS resolvable, AGENTS.md making it the preferred
  write form, so the narrowed grammar must accept aliases or this marker breaks wrongly.
- **14 name no resolvable id** — mostly a **deprecated 4-digit quad** (`c6ce`, `aa9e`,
  `adab`, `5169`, `1cef`, `48bd`, `85a5`) or a Jira id (`REB-640`), with
  `src/rebar/llm/config_readers.py:257` naming nothing. `tests/_child_hooks.py:1` DOES name
  `b939-bc68-1cb2-4ee9`, but on line 3, which the single-line grammar never reads; moving
  the id onto the marker line migrates it.

AGENTS.md deprecates the bare 4-digit quad because "in a store of any size those quads
collide, so they resolve to nothing." Those markers already cite an unresolvable ticket —
a sunset reference that means nothing, with nothing to detect it.

The baseline carries **647 mechanisms** (`.github/mechanism-baseline.json`), so the 90
admitted sit against ~557 grandfathered; this story governs the admitted set.

A marker-admitted new mechanism DOES land today: at `346a76f1c87`, `--check` reports
`active=647 new=32 increased=0 stale=0`, exit 0. Bug `a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a`, which once
made a new mechanism unlandable, is closed, though the docstring at
`src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:210-215` still claims otherwise. Half 2's precheck can
therefore be admitted by its own marker, so the ACs below are stated as exit codes rather
than as `new == 0`, which is not a reachable state.

## The change

Two halves.

**Half 1 — the marker names a sunset ticket.** Narrow the admission grammar so the third
field opens with a resolvable rebar ticket id rather than arbitrary prose. A marker whose
id does not resolve is no admission; the ratchet fails as it would for a blank reason.
"Resolvable" is a SHAPE check, not a store lookup: the grammar matches the alias,
two-quad, and four-quad forms the resolver accepts, and never opens the store.
`scripts/_mechanism_delta/` does no ticket resolution today, and `make lint` runs where the
`tickets` ref need not be fetched, so a lookup would add the dependency this story states
it avoids. A bare 4-digit quad is deprecated, so is not matched. A well-formed id naming
no existing ticket passes Half 1; Half 2 is what gives the id meaning. The id must sit on
the marker line, since the grammar reads one line.

**Half 2 — that ticket cannot close while the marker remains.** Add a deterministic
precheck to the completion-verification close path: when the ticket being closed is named
as the sunset ticket of a `# mechanism-ok:` marker still in the tree, the close is refused,
the refusal naming the marker's file plus line. Both ids are canonicalized before
comparison — the marker's and the one the close is invoked with — or the alias at
`_ref_lock.py:78` would never block its own close.

## What this retires

Required by `fe94`'s net-mechanism criterion; this is the first change judged by it.

This ADDS one deterministic close precheck and RETIRES the free-text reason as an
admission: afterwards only a resolvable ticket id admits a mechanism, so the "write any
sentence and pass" path at `compare.py:89-92` ceases to exist.

## Where the close refusal goes

The close gate has NO pluggable deterministic check — measured, not assumed: no
`_PRECHECKS` tuple and no precheck registry in `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`.
Plan review has `det_invariants.run_project_det_checks` driven by `exec: "DET"` overlay
entries; the close path has no equivalent.

The seam is the straight-line sequence in `_completion_precheck` (`:604`), whose refusals
run BEFORE the LLM verifier at `:694`. The landing check `_check_work_landed` (`:151`) is
called at `:685`, raising at `:215-222`; a new refusal is one more call there. Precedent
for reading state beyond git history: `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` (`:289`) reads landed
commits' diffs. The sunset scan reads tracked file contents — wider than any existing
precheck, stated not inferred.

## The --force caveat, stated rather than hidden

`_gate_skip_expectation` (`:554`, called at `:636`) short-circuits the ENTIRE precheck
block under `--force="<reason>"`, so no refusal in this gate is unconditional and the ACs
say "absent a human override". Per AGENTS.md agents must not use `--force`.

## Portability

Half 2 runs in-process in the close path, so it fires in any environment that can close a
ticket. Half 1 runs inside `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py`, whose trigger is the `make
lint` target rather than a CI provider, so it fires with no CI present. Both halves are
deterministic — neither calls an LLM, so no provider or model dependency arises.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Grammar, one test per case: `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits
      non-zero for a new mechanism whose marker reason does not open with a resolvable
      ticket id; non-zero for a bare 4-digit single-quad; zero for an alias; zero for a
      two- or four-quad id.
- [x] Close precheck, one test per case: closing a ticket named as the sunset ticket of a
      marker still present in the tree is refused absent a human `--force` override, with
      the error naming the marker's file plus line; closing that ticket succeeds once the
      marker is removed; closing a ticket named by no marker is unaffected.
- [x] Two invariants, one test each: removing a mechanism still passes the ratchet,
      guarding the shrink-only asymmetry at `compare.py:99` where `counters.stale` is
      never consulted; the new precheck fires with no CI environment configured.
- [x] All 14 real-site markers that do not name a resolvable id are migrated to one, with
      the remaining 76 (75 id + 1 alias) parsing under the narrowed grammar. Verified by
      `make verify`.
- [x] `make verify` passes.

## Measurement base

Every citation and count above was read from `origin/main` at `346a76f1c87`, where the
ratchet was also run. The 90/75/1/14 split was measured by parsing every site with
`parse_marker`, not sampled.
